paper-multi-module-explainable-artificia.summary: This paper proposes a multi-module explainable AI framework intended to improve transparency in project risk management decision-making, likely combining predictive modeling with interpretability methods. Evidence is limited to metadata, with no citing sentence or abstract available to clarify how the work engages with data generation techniques. It cites the CTGAN paper, but the manner of use (e.g., data augmentation, baseline, or mere citation) cannot be determined from the available evidence.
paper-multi-module-explainable-artificia.needs: Full text or citing sentence needed to determine whether CTGAN was run, used as a baseline, or merely cited in a related-work list.

paper-driven-synthetic-test-scenario-202.summary: This paper presents a modular AI-driven test automation architecture for web applications that combines a LLaMA4-based LLM for semantic form-field extraction, CTGAN for synthesizing realistic tabular test data (user records, credentials), and SeqGAN for generating ordered user-interaction scenarios, executed via Selenium WebDriver. Evaluated on five public web applications, the system achieves 95.05% format compliance in synthetic data and an 84.6% automated execution success rate. CTGAN, described via Xu et al.'s mode-specific normalization and conditional vectors, is trained directly on anonymized user records with explicit hyperparameters (embedding dimension, learning rates, epochs, batch size) to generate the synthetic test data that anchors the whole empirical evaluation.
paper-driven-synthetic-test-scenario-202.needs: Not fully certain whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package or an independent reimplementation was used; the described hyperparameters (embedding dimension, learning rates, epochs) closely match the library's constructor parameters, supporting api_user rather than port.

paper-asas-nanp-symposium-mathematical-2.summary: This paper proposes a rank-based method for generating synthetic databases with correlated, non-normal multivariate distributions to support predictive modeling in animal science, applied to ruminant methane emission data. It compares the rank-based method against copula-based approaches for preserving distribution moments and correlation structure, then trains random forest and linear regression models on the resulting synthetic datasets. SDV, TGAN, and CTGAN are cited in the related-work discussion as prior copula- and GAN-based synthetic data generation methods but are not run in the authors' experiments.

paper-addressing-scarcity-synthetic-secu.summary: This paper describes a cloud-based platform, built in collaboration with a Dutch telecommunications provider, that lets external synthetic-data vendors securely generate and validate synthetic data from schema input without accessing sensitive personal data, while enforcing GDPR compliance and re-identification checks. The platform was evaluated in an offline study with a TV viewership team, comparing vendor-generated synthetic datasets against agreed evaluation metrics. The original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper is cited only in the reference list, with no SDV component run or engaged with in the text.
paper-addressing-scarcity-synthetic-secu.needs: No full text obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV software itself was ever executed by any vendor or only cited as background literature.

paper-cancer-outcomes-synthetic-radiomic.summary: Observes that work on synthetic medical data has concentrated on generating images, from which radiomic features must then be extracted and which carry no prognostic information, and proposes instead to synthesize the radiomic features and the clinical record together so that a virtual patient is a single coherent row. Working from 132 non-small cell lung cancer patients in the public Lung1 cohort, the authors generate 106 virtual patients and train two-year overall survival models across four feature-selection methods and six classifiers, on real or synthetic data separately, testing on withheld real data and externally validating on a second cohort; XGBoost with random-forest importance features differs by under 1.3 percent between the two training sources. CTGAN is the only generator: version 0.13.0 is trained for 300 epochs with the Adam optimizer, its embedding and generator dimensions and learning rates are swept, constraints are specified to keep radiomic features standardized, ages non-negative and clinical features one-hot encoded, and fidelity is read off CTGAN's own built-in metric, one minus the Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic. The entire study therefore rests on running the SDV generator, down to its constraint interface and its packaged evaluation metric.

paper-comparative-analysis-augmentation-.summary: This conference paper evaluates eight data augmentation techniques -- including SMOTE variants, MixUp, and the generative models CTGAN and TVAE -- for improving minority-class (unsafe water) detection in an imbalanced water quality dataset, testing each across five classifiers. It finds that traditional oversampling (especially SMOTE-ENN) far outperforms CTGAN and TVAE in recall and training stability for this safety-critical task. CTGAN and TVAE are implemented by the authors themselves, with their own generator network described in prose, and run as underperforming generative baselines against which SMOTE-based methods are shown superior.
paper-comparative-analysis-augmentation-.needs: Not fully certain whether CTGAN/TVAE were built via the sdv-dev/ctgan package or entirely reimplemented from scratch; the prose describing 'our implementation employs a generator network' points to a self-built architecture (port) rather than api_user, per the reimplementation rule.

paper-membership-inference-utility-2025.summary: Tests the privacy claim made for synthetic tabular data by mounting membership inference attacks against it, in the healthcare and finance settings where the claim matters most. CTGAN, TVAE and GaussianCopula are the generators under attack, so all three of SDV's main synthesizers are the subject of an adversarial evaluation.

paper-imbalanced-fault-diagnosis-sample-.summary: A paper on fault diagnosis under class-imbalanced conditions, proposing a sample-weighted counterfactual approach to address minority-class fault detection, apparently in a chemical/process engineering context given the venue. No abstract or full text was available to describe the method's mechanics or experiments in detail. The work cites the CTGAN paper from the SDV family, but the manner of engagement cannot be determined from metadata alone.
paper-imbalanced-fault-diagnosis-sample-.needs: Full text or citing sentence needed to determine whether CTGAN is run (e.g., for oversampling minority fault classes) or merely cited in passing; industry assignment (chemicals_materials vs manufacturing) is inferred only from journal title.

paper-integrated-feature-temporal-gan-20.summary: This paper proposes IFT-GAN, a GAN-based framework for transaction fraud detection under severe class imbalance, combining a Feature-Aware Sample Selection module with a Temporal Dependency GAN using a novel Time-aware Gated Recurrent Unit to jointly refine feature space and model temporal dependencies in synthetic minority samples. Experiments on real-world and public datasets show IFT-GAN outperforms competing oversampling and generative methods. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing in the related-work discussion as prior work using conditional GANs to address column imbalance, without being run or compared experimentally.
paper-integrated-feature-temporal-gan-20.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so it is unverifiable whether CTGAN was actually run as a baseline in experiments beyond the related-work description.

paper-logicotab-controllable-tabular-syn.summary: This paper proposes LogiCoTab, a two-stage tabular data synthesis method that first uses a dual-module architecture to extract semantic features and inter-column logical relationships, then applies a diffusion-based generative model for controllable, conditional data synthesis, aiming to reduce logical inconsistencies seen in prior synthesizers. It is evaluated against numerous baselines including deep generative and diffusion-based tabular synthesizers on multiple public datasets using correlation-based fidelity metrics. CTGAN and TVAE are run as two of several comparison baselines in the experimental tables, consistently underperforming LogiCoTab on correlation-preservation metrics.
paper-logicotab-controllable-tabular-syn.needs: Implementation source (original SDV package vs. reimplementation) for CTGAN/TVAE baselines is not stated explicitly in the visible text.

paper-monitoring-welfare-individual-broi.summary: This paper presents a pilot study fitting broiler chickens with UWB and IMU wearable sensors to monitor activity, movement, and attachment-method effectiveness for welfare assessment on farms. It establishes practical guidelines on device attachment, retention time, and technical requirements (noise, UWB-IMU synergy) for individual-level poultry monitoring at scale. In its related-work discussion, it cites a prior study that trained CTGAN to generate additional data balancing three activity classes (active, inactive, sick) for identifying sick chickens from activity frequency, without running CTGAN themselves.
paper-monitoring-welfare-individual-broi.needs: The CTGAN use described is attributed to a cited prior study [6], not the authors' own experiments; this paper itself does not run CTGAN.

paper-ppmi-benchmark-parkinsons-2025.summary: Builds a paired benchmark over the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative cohort that evaluates longitudinal imputation methods and synthetic data generators on the same footing, adding sliced Wasserstein distance to the usual fidelity measures and reporting per-center results so that multi-center bias is visible rather than averaged away. Six generation methods are evaluated with the emphasis on CTGAN, whose mode-specific normalization and conditional generation the paper credits for handling mixed clinical data types, and the authors report that CTGAN gave the best preservation of the statistical properties of the PPMI data. Their contribution sits around the generator rather than inside it: the standard CTGAN implementation is run and then enhanced with clinical range constraints on the generated biomarker values, so SDV's CTGAN is the production generator of the framework.
paper-ppmi-benchmark-parkinsons-2025.needs: confirm api_user 4 against derivative_work 4. A second independent read of the same PDF found that the clinical-range term is added to CTGAN's loss (L_clinical, a sum of indicator functions over MCATOT in [0,30] and NP3TOT in [0,108]) rather than wrapping a frozen model, which fails the GAN_BERT wrapper test that separates api_user from derivative. Against that: no variant is named and the paper's own contribution is the benchmark rather than a generator. api_user 4 is retained here to match the STEAM ruling pending his call; rule this alongside the constrained-DGM and STEAM cases

paper-predicting-risk-programming-studen.summary: A conference paper addressing the problem of predicting at-risk programming students from small, imbalanced educational datasets, proposing the use of synthetic data generation to mitigate class imbalance. The approach appears to leverage synthetic oversampling techniques to improve classifier performance on minority (at-risk) student cases. CTGAN, cited from the original NeurIPS 2019 paper, is invoked as the synthetic data generation method underpinning this class-imbalance mitigation strategy.
paper-predicting-risk-programming-studen.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN (or the sdv-dev package) was actually run to generate synthetic student data or merely cited as related work. Integration and importance are inferred from the title's implication of synthetic data use for imbalance and should be verified against the full text.

paper-sos-shuffle-order-strategy-2025.summary: This paper proposes a data augmentation strategy for industrial Human Activity Recognition (HAR) that generates synthetic sensor data with an Attention Autoencoder (AAE) and CTGAN, then applies a random-sequence reordering (shuffle) to disrupt temporal dependencies and improve classification robustness, evaluated on the OpenPack logistics dataset. The CTGAN-generated dataset is one of the two synthetic-data sources compared against an AAE-generated dataset and the original data across augmentation orderings. SDV's CTGAN model is directly trained ('CTGAN from SDV... with 3 epochs') as one of the two synthetic data generators whose outputs anchor the whole empirical comparison.

paper-scalable-privacy-preserving-record.summary: This conference paper investigates integrating a Multibit Tree (MTB) indexing algorithm into Atyimo, a Brazilian privacy-preserving record linkage (PPRL) tool built on Spark, to improve scalability and execution time while preserving linkage accuracy on large administrative health databases. The authors evaluate their Spark DataFrame-based MTB implementation on simulated and real-world Brazilian health record datasets. To build one of the simulated evaluation datasets, they used the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) to generate synthetic birthdate values for simulated beneficiary records.
paper-scalable-privacy-preserving-record.needs: No specific SDV synthesizer or table metadata is named; only that SDV was used to generate a single field, so component-level engagement is minimal.

paper-pharmacogenetics-synthetic-2025.summary: Evaluates seven generation methods on pharmacogenetic profiles, spanning classical synthpop, the avatar method, copulas and a language-model approach. Three of the seven are SDV's, copulagan, ctgan and tvae, and the same group's earlier correlation-structure study appears in batch B, making this one of the more systematic external assessments of the library.

paper-most-suitable-sdg-2024.summary: Compares eleven generators drawn from three Python packages across thirteen tabular datasets, scoring each on utility, privacy and the fairness of models trained on its output, and concludes that CTGAN and PATE-CTGAN come closest to real data. SDV is one of the three packages under test and supplies the generator the study ends up recommending; the paper runs the library rather than citing it.

paper-actionability-synthetic-heterogene.summary: A cohort study of 3,735 adolescents and young adults with cancer that subsamples the population to varying sizes and generates synthetic data sets to study how sample size affects the veracity, utility, and privacy-concealment 'actionability' of synthetic health data. Four generator architectures built on the open-source Synthetic Data Vault library -- a speed-optimized Gaussian copula (Fast ML), a classical Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, and a DP-CGAN built atop SDV modules -- are each trained on 14 subsamples and compared on veracity/utility/privacy metrics, with SDMetrics' CAP algorithm used for the privacy concealment score. SDV's Gaussian Copula and CTGAN synthesizers are run directly as the core generators whose outputs the entire empirical study evaluates.
paper-actionability-synthetic-heterogene.needs: Full author affiliations/institutions were not given explicitly in the extracted text (only superscript numbers), so all affiliations are null.

paper-adflush-real-world-deployable-2024.summary: This paper presents AdFlush, a lightweight machine-learning classifier for browsers that detects advertisements and web trackers using a reduced set of 27 features, achieving higher accuracy and lower computational overhead than prior graph-based detectors like AdGraph and WebGraph. The authors also evaluate AdFlush's robustness against adversarial manipulation, including JavaScript obfuscation and synthetic feature perturbation. CTGAN is used to generate adversarial versions of the test dataset as one of three adversarial robustness scenarios, against which AdFlush's detection performance is measured.
paper-adflush-real-world-deployable-2024.needs: Evidence does not specify whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was used directly or via another implementation; treated as api_user given no reimplementation details are given.

paper-augmentation-class-imbalance-compe.summary: This paper addresses sensor drift and class imbalance in the Gas Sensor Array Drift Dataset by training MLP and SVM classifiers, and introduces a methodology using Conditional Tabular GANs to generate synthetic minority-class data and augment the training set. The generated data improved classification accuracy by up to 20% for minority-class compensation and over 10% for augmentation across several batches. CTGAN, described with its mode-specific normalization and variational Gaussian mixture model, is run as the sole generator producing all synthetic sensor data underpinning the empirical results.
paper-augmentation-class-imbalance-compe.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run directly or reimplemented, though the abstract strongly implies direct use of CTGAN as the generator.

paper-enhancing-business-analytics-tabul.summary: This paper introduces CBTabDM, a context-based diffusion model architecture for synthesizing tabular business data conditioned on user-supplied multi-dimensional context, aimed at supporting business decision-making beyond simple point estimates. It is evaluated on Yelp Reviews and Brazilian E-commerce datasets against an MLP baseline and CTGAN, with CBTabDM outperforming both on fidelity and utility metrics. CTGAN is run as the principal generative baseline throughout the quantitative and qualitative comparisons, but is noted as limited because it can only condition on a single discrete context feature.
paper-enhancing-business-analytics-tabul.needs: Unclear whether CTGAN was run via the sdv-dev/CTGAN package or the original authors' implementation, though results table treats it as a standard runnable baseline.

paper-enhancing-table-recognition-model-.summary: This paper proposes a data generation pipeline that analyzes structural characteristics of real tables and combines that analysis with a generative model to synthesize table images and their ground-truth labels, aiming to overcome the scarcity of large-scale table datasets. The synthesized data is used to fine-tune a Detection Transformer (DETR) model for table detection and table structure recognition, showing fast generation and labeling times. CTGAN is run as the content-generation component of the pipeline, fed with extracted table content to synthesize diverse cell contents for the generated table images.
paper-enhancing-table-recognition-model-.needs: Not fully clear whether the authors used the sdv-dev CTGAN package directly or a custom implementation; treated as api_user given no reimplementation details are given.

paper-gpu-optimization-techniques-accele.summary: This technical note presents GPU optimization strategies (mixed precision, data loading, kernel fusion, etc.) that yield a ~4.5x training speedup for optiGAN, a WGAN-GP model that generates multidimensional probability distributions of optical photons for radiation detector simulation. The work focuses purely on GPU engineering for this physics-simulation GAN and does not involve tabular data synthesis. TGAN is mentioned only once in the introduction as an example of GAN variants used for numerical data types, alongside other GAN applications, and appears in the reference list without further engagement.

paper-llm-gan-energy-load-2024.summary: Proposes DAPM-LLM, which converts residential building energy records into natural-language prompts so that a fine-tuned Bart model can predict energy usage, and pairs that with a tabular augmentation module because the source dataset holds only 768 samples. The augmentation is not SDV: the authors run Ashrapov's TabGan library, and CTGAN appears only in the survey of tabular GANs and in a background subsection crediting Xu et al. with mode-specific normalization for multimodal and non-Gaussian columns.

paper-machine-learning-ulcf-life-2024.summary: This paper develops machine-learning models to predict ultra-low-cycle-fatigue (ULCF) life of structural steels, using synthetic data generation to address limited experimental fatigue datasets. The metadata indicates the work cites the original TGAN paper (Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) as a reference for its synthetic data generation approach. No full text was available, so the exact role of TGAN in the pipeline (generator, baseline, or citation) cannot be confirmed.
paper-machine-learning-ulcf-life-2024.needs: Full text not available; cannot verify whether TGAN was actually run to generate synthetic fatigue data or merely cited as related work.

paper-synthcheck-dashboard-2024.summary: Observes that synthetic data quality tooling is mostly Python packages producing static reports, and builds SynthCheck, a graphical dashboard that walks a clinical user through resemblance, utility and privacy checks interactively, demonstrated on a cohort where missing values are first imputed by multiple imputation. Its survey of comparable tools opens with the Synthetic Data Vault, credited to Patki et al. and described through its SDGym and metrics modules as a package that both generates and evaluates synthetic data with a report but no interface, which is the gap SynthCheck fills. SDV is also one of the two generators run to produce the data the dashboard is demonstrated on, alongside HealthGAN, and is compared against it on correlation structure, outlier behaviour under local outlier factor, PCA variance and UMAP projections. SDV is therefore both a benchmark for the tool and the production generator of half its case study.

paper-step-deep-online-aggregation-2023.summary: This paper proposes 'evolving data frames' (edf), a novel data model enabling Online Aggregation (OLA) to be applied to nested, cascaded operations, and implements this in a system called Wake that produces converging estimates for complex query pipelines faster than existing OLA and non-OLA systems. CTGAN is cited only in passing, in a list of generative-model approaches to approximate query processing, and is never used or engaged with in the paper's own method or experiments.

paper-supervised-generative-optimization.summary: This paper proposes SC-GOAT, a synthetic tabular data generation framework that adds a supervised, downstream-task-aware component to existing generators and uses Bayesian optimization plus meta-learning to find an optimal mixture of several synthetic data distributions. The empirical work fits Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, CopulaGAN, and TVAE from the SDV package as the individual base synthesizers whose outputs are weighted and combined, and compares the mixture against CTAB-GAN+ and each individual model on Adult and credit datasets. SDV's synthesizers (Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, CopulaGAN, TVAE) are run directly from the SDV package as the core generators whose weighted combination constitutes the paper's whole empirical contribution.

paper-advanced-machine-learning-runtime-.summary: A research-vision paper proposing to investigate whether generative models can produce realistic synthetic failure or intrusion data to support dependability research, motivated by the cost and expertise required for fault/intrusion injection techniques. It surveys the landscape of generative modeling for sequential, image, and tabular data without running any experiments itself. CTGAN is cited once in passing as an example of remarkable recent results in synthetic data generation, with no further engagement in the text.
paper-advanced-machine-learning-runtime-.needs: None; single passing citation confirmed absent elsewhere in full text.

paper-evaluating-utility-gan-generated-2.summary: This conference paper compares SMOTE, ADASYN, and GAN-based synthetic tabular data generation for addressing class imbalance and low-resource training-data scenarios in binary classification tasks, using recall as the primary evaluation metric. The authors train and evaluate CTGAN and CopulaGAN, explicitly identified as models 'from the Synthetic Data Vault ecosystem,' assessing their synthetic data quality via KSTest and detection scores before selecting CopulaGAN's output to run the class-balancing and low-resource experiments. SDV's CTGAN and CopulaGAN are run directly as the generators whose synthetic output the entire empirical evaluation is built on.

paper-fraudammo-large-scale-synthetic-20.summary: This paper introduces FraudAmmo, a large-scale (3M transaction) synthetic payment-fraud dataset generated with a differentially-private variant of CTAB-GAN, released to address the scarcity of open, privacy-preserving fraud benchmarks. The authors describe CTGAN's mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling as the techniques CTAB-GAN builds upon, but the generator actually run is CTAB-GAN, not CTGAN itself. For privacy evaluation they compute the Categorical Correct Attribution Probability, explicitly noting it is 'an evaluation metric that is included in the SDMetrics package,' making SDMetrics one of the tools used to quantify the synthetic dataset's privacy preservability.
paper-fraudammo-large-scale-synthetic-20.needs: SDMetrics use is confirmed for one privacy metric (CategoricalCAP); unclear whether other SDMetrics-based metrics (e.g., NNDR, statistical similarity scores) were also drawn from the package, since the text does not fully enumerate their sources.

paper-generating-synthetic-personal-heal.summary: This paper proposes DP-CGANS, a differentially private conditional GAN for generating realistic and privacy-preserving personal health data, addressing class imbalance and variable dependency through a conditional vector and separate transformation of categorical and continuous variables, with DP noise injected into gradients during training. The architecture described -- mode-specific normalization, conditioning on minority classes, and a conditional vector -- closely follows CTGAN's design, which the authors extend into a new differentially private model.
paper-generating-synthetic-personal-heal.needs: Full text not available; the paper cites tgan-2018 but the described conditional-vector and mode-specific-normalization design matches CTGAN more closely -- possible mis-citation or conflation between TGAN and CTGAN that cannot be resolved from the abstract alone.

paper-rc-tgan-relational-2023.summary: Observes that synthesizing a relational database means reproducing the relationships between tables, not only each table's own distribution. RC-TGAN extends the tabular GAN with row-level conditioning on parent rows, making it a direct competitor to HMA built on the first-party generator.

paper-smart-meter-synthetic-generator-20.summary: This software impacts paper presents a Python-based GUI tool that uses the Facebook Prophet forecasting library to generate prediction-based synthetic smart meter time-series data, addressing the difficulty of obtaining real smart meter data due to privacy restrictions. The tool is intended to help researchers test smart grid data analytics algorithms without access to real consumer data. SDV's original 2016 paper is cited only in the reference list as related prior work on synthetic data generation, with no engagement in the body text.

paper-generating-semi-synthetic-datasets.summary: This paper presents DGIDS, a framework that produces semi-synthetic network intrusion detection datasets by blending generated attack/benign traffic with real regular traffic collected from a local network, improving downstream NIDS detection accuracy from 54% to 90.39% in experiments. To generate the synthetic tabular network flow data, the authors build a model called AADG explicitly derived from CTGAN's conditional GAN design, reusing its approach of uniformly sampling discrete-column values during training to preserve real data distributions. CTGAN's conditional generative adversarial network architecture is the foundation from which their own named synthetic-data generator is built.
paper-generating-semi-synthetic-datasets.needs: Unclear whether AADG reuses SDV's actual CTGAN code (would be derivative_work/api_user) or is a from-scratch reimplementation of CTGAN's conditional-vector mechanism (would be port); text describes the mechanism in prose without naming the sdv-dev package.

paper-wood-identification-cyclobalanopsi.summary: This paper proposes a wood-species identification pipeline for the genus Cyclobalanopsis that trains SVM and BPNN classifiers on microscopic vessel and wood-fiber cell geometric features, using LIME to interpret which features drive species prediction. To overcome limited real samples, the authors train CTGAN models on the real cell geometry data to generate large simulated datasets (1000 synthetic samples per species per cell type) that are then used to train and boost the classifiers' accuracy, evaluating synthetic data fidelity with the KSComplement statistic. CTGAN is run as the core data-generation engine underpinning the entire empirical pipeline, with its conditional generator/discriminator design and quality metrics (KSComplement) driving the whole augmentation and evaluation programme.
paper-wood-identification-cyclobalanopsi.needs: Not fully clear whether CTGAN and the KSComplement metric were run via the sdv-dev/SDMetrics packages or a custom reimplementation; no explicit library name or hyperparameter table shown in the extracted passages.

paper-multi-dimensional-evaluation-synth.summary: This paper defines four evaluation dimensions -- attribute, bivariate, population, and application fidelity -- for assessing the utility of synthetic data generators, and applies representative metrics from each dimension to compare four data synthesizers (Datasynthesizer, Synthpop parametric, Synthpop nonparametric, and SDV) across 19 real datasets of varying size and feature count. It also studies correlations among the chosen metrics to see whether a single metric could serve as a general utility indicator. The Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), described as a copula-based generator using a Gaussian Copula to model joint attribute distributions, is run as one of the four synthesizers benchmarked throughout the study.

paper-alphaqo-robust-learned-query-2022.summary: AlphaQO is a reinforcement-learning-based framework that trains robust learned query optimizers by having a query generator learn to produce 'difficult' queries that expose weaknesses in the optimizer, iteratively improving it with far fewer queries than random generation. The paper's empirical focus is on query plan cost estimation and RL-based query generation for database systems, not on synthetic tabular data. TGAN, the SDV-family deep generative model for tabular data, appears only in the citation list with no visible engagement in the retrieved evidence.
paper-alphaqo-robust-learned-query-2022.needs: No citing sentence or full text obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN is discussed, used, or merely listed among related generative models for query workload generation.

paper-generative-adversarial-networks-mo.summary: This paper develops custom GAN architectures, including conditional GANs, to model univariate and joint distributions of diabetes-relevant clinical biomarkers for under-represented race/ethnicity groups using NHANES data, comparing generated outputs to held-out test data. The generators and discriminators are built from scratch as simple dense neural networks rather than using an existing package. CTGAN is cited among the GAN literature informing the conditional GAN approach used to model race/ethnicity-specific biomarker profiles, but the evidence does not show the SDV package itself being run.
paper-generative-adversarial-networks-mo.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was cited merely as related conditional-GAN work or engaged with more substantively in the related-work section.

paper-privetab-2022.summary: Releases network event data for research by replacing it with synthetic records that keep analytical value, adding t-closeness sampling and SHA-256 encryption of quasi-identifiers on top. CTGAN is the generator: trained on the real data, then sampled repeatedly until the Earth Mover's Distance for every attribute falls below the privacy threshold.

paper-browser-fingerprinting-dp-2021.summary: Shows that a browser can be identified from network traffic features alone, then asks what it costs to defend the resulting model and its training data with differential privacy, comparing DP-SGD on the classifier against releasing a differentially private synthetic dataset instead. The synthetic-data arm runs PATE-CTGAN together with QUAIL: PATE-CTGAN is Rosenblatt et al.'s CTGAN variant that trains the generator under the PATE framework, so the paper's privacy-preserving dataset is produced by a named third-party CTGAN descendant.
paper-browser-fingerprinting-dp-2021.needs: Same convention gap as paper-nft-data-trading-dpctgan-2025 (shard 55): a named third-party CTGAN derivative is run as the production generator rather than benchmarked. Recorded api_user 4 to match that precedent; `inherited` 3 is the alternative. This is now the second instance, so the ruling settles a recurring pattern rather than a one-off

paper-conditional-deep-convolutional-gen.summary: This paper proposes a Conditional Deep Convolutional GAN (CDCGAN) for guided generation of isolated handwritten Arabic characters, addressing the scarcity of labeled handwritten Arabic datasets. Evaluated via MS-SSIM and machine learning efficacy tests, CDCGAN produces synthetic characters comparable to real samples and performs reasonably well against similar work on tabular data generation. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni) is cited only in a bibliographic comparison to prior GAN-based tabular data synthesis work, with no code run.
paper-conditional-deep-convolutional-gen.needs: Full text not available; only abstract-level citing sentences seen, so depth of engagement with TGAN cannot be fully confirmed.

paper-restore-neural-completion-relation.summary: This paper proposes ReStore, a system for automated relational data completion in incomplete databases, using neural schema-structured autoregressive models to synthesize missing tuples and reduce bias in OLAP aggregate query results. The evaluation is entirely built on the authors' own autoregressive completion models, not on SDV code. TGAN is cited only in passing as one of several prior deep-learning approaches to tuple synthesis.

paper-challenges-machine-learning-applie.summary: This paper is a methodological safety-hazard analysis across the machine-learning lifecycle for safety-critical cyber-physical systems, illustrated with an autonomous shop-floor transportation vehicle scenario. It surveys risks in data collection, training, and deployment of ML-based control systems, referencing many prior works including approaches to non-representative training data. It mentions the Synthetic Data Vault only in passing, as a citation for automatic synthetic dataset generation techniques, without running or evaluating it.

paper-ctgan-load-forecasting-2020.summary: Short-term load forecasting is limited by how little external feature data utilities hold, so this proposes a two-stage scheme that generates the missing features before forecasting. CTGAN is trained on the input variables and sampled to produce them, and is the generation model the scheme is built on.

paper-generating-high-fidelity-cybersecu.summary: This conference paper proposes using Generative Adversarial Networks to synthesize high-fidelity cybersecurity data, aiming to overcome the scarcity of shareable, realistic datasets of nominal and adversarial activity for training cyber-defense machine learning models. The authors train a GAN discriminator on real-world data and describe generating synthetic samples for benchmarking detection systems. The work cites the TGAN paper as prior art on GAN-based generation of tabular data, without evidence in the available text that TGAN itself was run or benchmarked.
paper-generating-high-fidelity-cybersecu.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN code was actually run as a baseline or only cited as related work, so integration and importance are best-effort estimates from the abstract and metadata alone.

paper-synthetic-minority-oversampling-vi.summary: This paper introduces actGAN, a WGAN-GP-based oversampling method with an activation-specific generator output layer designed for extremely imbalanced, mixed-type vital statistics data, applied to predicting early stillbirth from Finnish birth registry data. actGAN is compared against SMOTE-NC and cost-sensitive baselines and shown to improve true positive rate at clinically significant false positive rates. TGAN, an LSTM-based generator for tabular data, is cited only in passing as prior related work on GAN methods for tabular data, not used or benchmarked.
paper-synthetic-minority-oversampling-vi.needs: None; TGAN mention is clearly a brief related-work description, not an experimental use.

paper-opening-internet-monopolies-compet.summary: A policy brief examining how mandating that dominant internet firms share user data with competitors and academia could curb data-driven market power and spread the benefits of AI more widely, while weighing the resulting risks to privacy and security. The paper is a policy analysis rather than a technical study, with no described experiments or generative modeling of its own. It cites the original Synthetic Data Vault paper, likely in the context of synthetic data as a privacy-preserving mechanism for data sharing.
paper-opening-internet-monopolies-compet.needs: Full text not obtained; the specific sentence citing SDV and its context (e.g., synthetic data as a privacy-preserving data-sharing mechanism) could not be verified.

preprint-pipeline-realistic-synthetic-lo.summary: This preprint presents a pipeline for generating synthetic longitudinal electronic health record data by extending the HALO and ConSequence frameworks with a post-processing step that reconstructs continuous variables and timestamps, evaluated across three clinically diverse datasets for realism and downstream utility. CTGAN is cited only in passing as one of several generative adversarial approaches to synthetic data generation in the background discussion, and is never run or engaged with further in the pipeline itself.

preprint-benders-solution-strategies-sto.summary: This preprint develops Benders-decomposition-based solution strategies for stochastic capacity expansion planning models that incorporate loss-of-load-probability (LOLP) chance constraints, targeting power system reliability and investment planning under uncertainty. No abstract or full text was available to determine how synthetic data methods factor into the modeling or experiments. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper, but the evidence gives no indication that SDV's software was run rather than merely referenced.
preprint-benders-solution-strategies-sto.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV is run, adopted conceptually, or merely cited in the reference list. Use case and any synthesizer/concept usage cannot be determined from metadata alone.

preprint-comedbench-multi-source-benchma.summary: CoMedBench is a reproducible benchmark evaluating a family of synthetic-data generators across 37 tabular and temporal downstream clinical-prediction tasks drawn from seven public healthcare data sources (MIMIC-III/IV, eICU, UCI, NHANES, BRFSS, pycox). It compares statistical fidelity and downstream utility of CTGAN-, TVAE-, CopulaGAN-, and GaussianCopula-based generators (named CoMed-CTGAN, CoMed-TVAE, CoMed-CopulaGAN, CoMed-GaussianCopula) trained on the same data. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, CopulaGAN and GaussianCopula synthesizers are run directly as the four generators whose fidelity and downstream utility form the entire empirical comparison.
preprint-comedbench-multi-source-benchma.needs: Paper cites SDV's original 2016 paper (Patki, Wedge, Veeramachaneni) and CTGAN 2019, and runs CopulaGAN/GaussianCopula which are SDV-only models, but the text never explicitly names the 'sdv' Python package or import statements, so the exact library provenance (sdv vs a reimplementation) is inferred from model names rather than stated directly.

paper-sgn-distribution-shift-2026.summary: Trains a generator on a source domain to produce samples aligned with a shifted target domain by learning a shared linear space and a transmission between the two, so that a handful of target samples is enough to augment the target domain usefully, demonstrated on both image and tabular benchmarks. CTGAN and TVAE are the two tabular baselines, implemented from the SDV library with the default structures it states, and the paper attributes their weaker downstream regression and classification results to their being fitted to the source distribution alone.

paper-disjunctive-refinement-layer-2025.summary: Introduces the Disjunctive Refinement Layer, which maps a generator's output into the region defined by quantifier-free linear formulas, so that background knowledge expressing non-convex or disconnected admissible spaces is satisfied by construction rather than by rejection sampling; constraint satisfaction becomes guaranteed and downstream efficacy improves. The layer is attached to five deep generative models, CTGAN and TVAE among them, giving CTGAN+DRL and TVAE+DRL, which are compared against the unmodified models and against the earlier linear-inequality layer from the same group.

preprint-flow-feedback-driven-synthetic-.summary: This paper introduces FLOW, a synthetic longitudinal dataset of 1,000 individuals over two years, generated by a rule-based, feedback-driven simulation modeling interactions between workload, lifestyle behaviors, and wellbeing at daily resolution. It also releases a configurable generation tool for reproducible experimentation, positioning FLOW as an alternative to GAN-based tabular synthesis methods that prioritize distributional similarity over temporal coherence. CTGAN is cited only in passing as an example of prior GAN-based tabular data synthesis work, with no library run or model used.

preprint-handling-extreme-class-imbalanc.summary: This paper builds machine learning models (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM) to predict rare suicide-attempt cases from a small, extremely imbalanced clinical dataset, using a Conditional GAN of the authors' own design to synthesize additional positive samples for data augmentation. The related-work section cites CTGAN as an example of GAN-based tabular data augmentation and describes the conditional-GAN concept of generating data conditioned on a label, but the paper's own augmentation model is separately implemented rather than the SDV package. CTGAN is cited only as prior art illustrating conditional generation of tabular data, with no code from the library run.
preprint-handling-extreme-class-imbalanc.needs: Confirms citation-only use: CTGAN is described conceptually as prior conditional-GAN work but never run; the paper's own GAN augmentation appears to be a custom implementation, not the sdv-dev package.

paper-health-uncertainty-riga-2025.summary: Proposes RIGA, which converts small imbalanced clinical tables into image representations so that image generative models can augment them, then converts back for tabular classifiers, tested on a preterm-birth cohort and a myocardial infarction dataset where the minority class is very small. CTGAN is the tabular augmentation baseline the image route is measured against, reported as reducing AUC on some datasets and giving a modest 0.87 per cent improvement on another, and named as the tabular GAN the authors' approach outperforms.

preprint-cooling-guide-diffusion-model-2.summary: This preprint proposes a cooling-guided denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) that generates battery cell layouts optimized for feasibility, diversity, and cooling efficiency in immersion-cooled battery packs, replacing slow iterative FE-simulation-based design. The authors benchmark their model against TabDDPM and against CTGAN trained on the same 700,000-layout dataset, showing their DDPM achieves a Composite Quality Index roughly 66 times higher than CTGAN. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run as one of two state-of-the-art comparison baselines and is outperformed on feasibility and cooling efficiency.

preprint-high-precision-medical-speech-2.summary: This paper presents United-MedASR, an ASR architecture for the clinical domain that combines synthetic vocabulary generation from sources like ICD-10, MIMS, and FDA databases with fine-tuning of Whisper, Faster Whisper inference, and a BART-based semantic enhancer to reduce word error rates on medical terminology. The system is evaluated on LibriSpeech, Europarl-ASR, Tedlium, and FLEURS benchmarks. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in passing as a reference for de-anonymisation risk when discussing ethical concerns around synthetic data in medical applications, with no SDV component actually run.

preprint-tabular-generation-binary-diffu.summary: This paper introduces a lossless binary transformation for tabular data and a new diffusion-based generative model, Binary Diffusion, that uses XOR noise operations and binary cross-entropy loss to avoid the complex preprocessing typical of tabular generators. It evaluates the new model against several state-of-the-art baselines on datasets like Travel, Adult Income, and Diabetes, showing smaller model size and competitive or better performance. TVAE, CopulaGAN, and CTGAN from the SDV family are run as baseline generators, trained with default settings (batch size 500, 200 epochs) alongside GReaT and Distill-GReaT for comparison.

preprint-can-you-rely-your-2023.summary: This NeurIPS 2023 paper introduces 3S Testing, a deep generative modeling framework that produces synthetic test sets to improve evaluation of ML models on underrepresented subgroups and under simulated distributional shifts, showing it outperforms real-test-data baselines in estimating minority-subgroup performance. The framework's main experiments rely on CTGAN as the underlying generative model, chosen for its conditional generation of subgroup- or shift-specific data, and it is also compared against TVAE and normalizing flows as alternative base generators. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as the core generator throughout the paper's empirical programme, leveraging its conditional sampling mechanism for subgroup and shift simulation.
preprint-can-you-rely-your-2023.needs: Text also references 'Patki 2016' as a pre-implemented generative library but this is not listed among cited SDV papers; not scored as separate use.

paper-tabsyn-latent-diffusion-2023.summary: Argues that diffusion applied directly to mixed-type tables must contend with one-hot categorical columns that do not diffuse well, and proposes TabSyn, which first learns a joint continuous latent space with a transformer variational autoencoder and then runs score-based diffusion inside it, so that a single Gaussian process covers numerical and categorical columns at once and sampling needs few steps. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE baselines among the seven methods it is measured against across six datasets.

preprint-overconfidence-dangerous-thing-.summary: This paper proposes HAMP, a defense against membership inference attacks (MIAs) that forces machine learning models to produce low-confidence, high-entropy predictions during and after training, without needing extra data. The authors show HAMP achieves strong membership privacy alongside high accuracy across five benchmark datasets, outperforming seven state-of-the-art MIA defenses. CTGAN is mentioned in a body sentence about modeling tabular data, but the full-text search found the SDV-family reference occurs only in the bibliographic citation, not as an actually run component.
preprint-overconfidence-dangerous-thing-.needs: The extracted body sentence claims CT-GAN is used for tabular data modeling, yet the full-text search finding says the SDV reference appears only in the bibliography; this contradiction could not be resolved from the given evidence.

preprint-survtimesurvival-survival-analy.summary: This paper proposes a Transformer-based survival analysis model that handles time-varying covariates and integrates synthetic data generation (via a SurvivalGAN-based technique) to address data sparsity in survival datasets, evaluated on three public medical datasets. The method combines a new Transformer architecture with the SurvTrace model and a SurvivalGAN-style synthetic data component to improve survival prediction accuracy. CTGAN is cited only in the bibliography as prior work on conditional GAN modeling of tabular data, with no evidence it was run in the reported experiments.

preprint-gan-tabular-generator-construct.summary: This preprint surveys and analyzes the evolution of tabular GAN architectures (table-GAN, TGAN, CTGAN, CTAB-GAN, DATGAN) for constructing data synopses used in Approximate Query Processing, detailing how each handles mixed data types, multimodal distributions, and imbalance, and it proposes a suite of statistical metrics adapted for evaluating the fidelity of GAN-generated synopses. CTGAN and TGAN's architectures (conditional generator, training-by-sampling, VGM-based mode encoding) are described in depth as prior art the paper builds its taxonomy on, while the SDMetrics library's KS-statistic and TVD metrics are described and reformed for the paper's own synopsis-quality metrics. SDV's CTGAN component and the SDMetrics quality-report metrics are engaged with descriptively and adapted rather than shown to be executed via the library itself.
preprint-gan-tabular-generator-construct.needs: No passage shows the CTGAN/TGAN library or SDMetrics package actually being invoked with code/parameters; unclear whether experiments ran the sdv-dev/SDMetrics packages or the authors only reimplemented/adapted the described formulas.

preprint-patient-centric-synthetic-gener.summary: This preprint introduces 'Avatar', a patient-centric, local-model-based method for generating individual-level synthetic data from sensitive biomedical datasets while preserving privacy, tested on an HIV clinical trial and the Wisconsin Breast Cancer dataset. It evaluates re-identification risk with distance-based privacy metrics and shows statistical utility is retained versus original data. SDV (The Synthetic Data Vault) and the TGAN tabular GAN paper appear only in the reference list among related synthetic data generation approaches, with no engagement or use in the method or experiments.

paper-promptehr-records-2022.summary: Casts synthetic electronic health record generation as conditional language modelling: PromptEHR encodes a patient's demographics and prior visits as prompts to an encoder-decoder language model, so that longitudinal multimodal visit sequences can be generated and evaluated by perplexity rather than by tabular similarity alone. CTGAN is the tabular-generation prior art the design departs from, cited for the observation that GANs and VAEs struggle with multimodal non-Gaussian distributions and sparse one-hot vectors, and named among the conditional-GAN approaches that generate only static tabular records.

paper-sequential-2022.summary: Documents the PAR algorithm used for multi-sequence time series in SDV: context columns are modeled separately from the sequence body, allowing generation of new entities with their own coherent sequences.

thesis-what-you-see-what-2018.summary: This dissertation combines computer vision, statistical analysis, and urban design methods to relate spatial features to patterns of spatial use, using case studies in Madrid and Pittsburgh with bivariate analysis and machine-learning-based spatial clustering. It proposes a data-informed design framework to help practitioners and policymakers explore urban scenarios. SDV's foundational paper (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only in passing to support a general claim that synthetic data can now match real data quality without compromising privacy.
thesis-what-you-see-what-2018.needs: Only abstract and citing sentence available; full text not obtained, so it's unclear whether SDV software was ever used or only cited rhetorically in the literature review.

repo-asi.summary: Polish-language course material on AI solution architectures and deployment methodologies, with several student project templates. SDV recurs across those projects: `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` and `SingleTableMetadata` in one test harness, `sdv==1.9.0` pinned in another environment, `ctgan` and `copulas` in a tracked experiment run. SDV as a standard component of an MLOps teaching pipeline.

repo-user2024-anonymisation.summary: Material for a three-hour useR! 2024 tutorial in Salzburg on anonymising data for open science, worked through the R packages sdcMicro, simPop and synthpop. CTGAN gets two slides of its own in the presentation source, introducing it as a conditional tabular GAN for realistic synthetic data and explaining why it exists — handling the mixed numeric and categorical types that defeat simpler methods. SDV's model is described to an official-statistics audience; the tutorial's own code is R and runs none of it.
